review.thesis: The verdict changes what Muntin sells from software to a professional deliverable, and it does that without once using the words legal, counsel, licence, regulation, insurance, liability, indemnity, LLC or tax — I grepped the full verdict JSON and the counts are zero for every one of those. It handles exactly one legal question (employer consent to publish a specimen) and none of the other eight the pivot creates. Two of those are potentially disqualifying as written. First, the framing: Maryland's practice-of-accountancy definition reaches "providing a written certificate or opinion offering positive or negative assurance … on the correctness of the information or on the fairness of the presentation of the information in a financial statement, report, schedule, or an exhibit," with civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation [UNVERIFIED — secondary sources, needs the statutory text confirmed]. The verdict's own words are "a dated, signed statement … sold the way an audit firm sells an opinion," plus a "signed Ed25519 workpaper export." A nonlicensee may prepare financial statements *without issuing a report*, and COMAR 09.24.01.10 appears to give a compilation safe harbour if the report carries "The preparer of this report has not undergone and is not required to undergo peer review" and never references SSARS — so the commercial promise survives, but only if the words change. The framing that makes the strategy sellable is the framing that puts it at the licensing line. Second, and nobody has caught this: the strategy's delivery mechanism is "an agent-run exception desk" in which sessions author vendor templates from the invoices the deterministic engine could not read. That is an LLM reading customer invoice content. `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3888` publishes "Your invoice content never reaches a language model," `:3082` adds "we have no model to train," 93 storefront pages carry the claim, and `docs/sub-processors.md` states "The deterministic v4 architecture removed the LLM sub-processor (Anthropic) entirely; no third party processes invoice content." The plan discloses the desk on `/close/` and nowhere in the DPA, the sub-processor list, or the ROPA — turning the company's single load-bearing honesty claim into a false one at the exact moment it is sold as the product. Underneath both sits an entity that three documents describe three different ways: `LICENSE` says Muntin Digital LLC, `/home/user/potentially-profitable/terms.html:423` says "a Maryland LLC," `docs/tos.md:135` says Delaware is "Muntin Digital LLC's home state," and `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:359` asks the founder for "confirmation an entity EXISTS (if the product is currently operated as a sole proprietorship, counsel should advise on entity formation FIRST — it gates everything)" — a checklist item that has sat open since roughly 2026-06-09. Signing a number personally, out of an entity whose existence and state are unconfirmed, against a valuation the audit already establishes is biased low three ways, is the precise fact pattern that produces personal liability. The strategy is right that credibility is the closing asset. It has not noticed that a signature is a legal instrument, not a design flourish.

neglected.issue: The deliverable's framing sits on the Maryland attest/report line, and the verdict picked the riskiest available words on purpose
neglected.evidence: The verdict says the product is "a dated, signed statement of food cost … sold the way an audit firm sells an opinion," grafts a "signed Ed25519 workpaper export," and adopts the positioning "Every leg foots, or we withhold the number." Maryland Bus. Occ. & Prof. Title 2 / COMAR 09.24 define practice of certified public accountancy to include "providing a written certificate or opinion offering positive or negative assurance … on the correctness of the information or on the fairness of the presentation of the information in a financial statement, report, schedule, or an exhibit"; the Board may assess civil penalties up to $5,000 per violation. A nonlicensee may perform "the preparation of financial statements without the issuance of reports," and COMAR 09.24.01.10 appears to exempt a compilation whose report says "The preparer of this report has not undergone and is not required to undergo peer review" and does not reference SSARS. [UNVERIFIED — secondary sources; statutory text and the Board's current position must be confirmed.] The verdict contains zero occurrences of licence/regulation/counsel/attorney.
neglected.consequence: Inventory valuation and food cost are exactly "a schedule" and "an exhibit." A Board complaint — most plausibly filed by the very CPA the strategy courts as reviewer — would not need to prove harm, only that a nonlicensee issued a signed report offering assurance on the correctness of financial information for a fee. The entire GTM (CPA as gatekeeper) puts the complainant in the room by design.

neglected.issue: The agent-run exception desk makes Anthropic an undisclosed sub-processor and falsifies the company's single load-bearing claim
neglected.evidence: The verdict's delivery model is "an agent-run exception desk … A session may author a vendor template, a pack-parse mapping, a catalog synonym" — which requires the session to read the customer invoice the deterministic engine failed on. Against that: `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3888` "Your invoice content never reaches a language model"; `:3082` "we have no model to train"; `:4067` "We do not read your invoices with a language model"; 93 storefront HTML files carry the claim; `docs/marketing-claims.md` lists it first under "Verified — say these freely (they are the spine)"; `docs/sub-processors.md` states "The deterministic v4 architecture removed the LLM sub-processor (Anthropic) entirely; no third party processes invoice content." The plan's only disclosure is prose on `/close/`. Sub-processor list, DPA §6, ROPA A2 and the DPIA are untouched.
neglected.consequence: DPA §6 requires 30 days' advance notice of a new sub-processor with a right to terminate, and `docs/sub-processors.md` states that once paying customers exist "no founder override" is available — so the desk cannot legally start on day one of the first paying month. Independently, an unqualified present-tense claim contradicted by the delivery mechanism is a textbook FTC §5 deception, and the buyer's own professional adviser is the person most likely to test it. The company would be caught doing the one thing its brand exists to promise it never does.

neglected.issue: No entity is confirmed, and the two customer-facing legal documents name different states
neglected.evidence: `LICENSE` (product repo): "Copyright (c) 2026 Muntin Digital LLC." `/home/user/potentially-profitable/terms.html:423`: "Muntin Digital™ is a Maryland LLC … registered in Silver Spring, MD; the LLC's registered agent is on file with the Maryland Department of Assessments & Taxation," and `:475` sets Maryland governing law. `docs/tos.md:135-137`: governed by "the State of Delaware (Muntin Digital LLC's home state)" with disputes in Delaware courts. `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:359` still asks the founder to supply "legal entity name, type, state of formation, registered agent, EIN; confirmation an entity EXISTS."
neglected.consequence: If the entity is Maryland-only, the Delaware forum and governing-law clause in the product ToS is unenforceable boilerplate that a first customer's counsel will strike, and the ToS a court reads is the storefront's retired services terms. If no entity exists, or a Delaware LLC is transacting in Maryland without foreign qualification, the liability shield the founder is relying on when he personally signs a number may not be there. An LLC in any case does not shield a member from his own negligent misrepresentation — it shields him from the entity's debts.

neglected.issue: Third-party reliance is outside the contract, and no limitation-of-liability clause reaches it
neglected.evidence: The buyer's stated readers are the owner, the bookkeeper, and "the CPA who must not be able to dismantle the number." `docs/tos.md` §6 caps liability at 12 months of fees and is a click-through SaaS agreement between Muntin and the account holder. Maryland has expanded negligent-misrepresentation duty beyond privity, and most jurisdictions apply Restatement (Second) of Torts §552 to reach a limited class of intended users of a client's financial statements [UNVERIFIED — needs Maryland-specific confirmation]. Meanwhile the audit establishes the number is biased low three ways, `apps/api/src/lib/inventory-reconcile.ts:249` is an empty `if (estimated) {}`, `apps/api/src/lib/inventory-purchases-store.ts:19-20` documents "No location filter" against per-location counts, and the Cost-Index market prior values inventory at a public wholesale median that `docs/audits/panels/operator-domain-correctness.md:25` says ASC 330 does not permit as a book basis.
neglected.consequence: A $600/month fee caps contract exposure at $7,200. It caps nothing owed to a lender, an SBA underwriter, a buyer in a sale, or an insurer on a business-interruption claim who relied on a signed inventory figure. A signed statement is precisely the artifact that creates the limited class of intended users §552 reaches, and Muntin would be signing one it knows is biased low.

neglected.issue: E&O is cheap for a bookkeeper and likely excluded for what the verdict describes
neglected.evidence: Market rates for solo bookkeeper professional liability run roughly $37-56/month, ~$440-700/year at $1M/$1M [UNVERIFIED — broker quotes needed]. But standard bookkeeper/miscellaneous-professional forms exclude services requiring a licence the insured does not hold, and public audit is commonly not an eligible practice area; coverage for audit/review/compilation is a specialised, separately underwritten add-on. `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:150-155` has had "the founder will engage a broker (Embroker, Vouch, etc.)" open since 2026-06-09 with no quote on file, and `runbooks/v6-pivot-plan.md:70` contemplates $70-115k of personal capital.
neglected.consequence: The application question — "do you issue signed reports or opinions on financial information?" — is answered by the verdict's own positioning. Answer yes and the cheap policy is declined or the attest exclusion bites; answer no and the policy is voidable for misrepresentation at exactly the claim that triggers it. The verdict's framing and the affordable insurance are mutually exclusive, and nobody has priced that trade.

neglected.issue: The employer repair covers publication only, not the fifteen months of use, the IP, or the moonlighting question
neglected.evidence: The verdict's graft is "written authorization from ownership, or a redacted specimen, or a consenting third restaurant" — scoped to the specimen close. It does not touch: the 919-invoice corpus of Tacombi vendor invoices that `docs/audits/company-audit-2026-08-07-appendices/lens-upside.md:13` calls the moat; real Tacombi strings still sitting in `services/extract/tests/golden/real_fixtures/` (`fresco_merged_header.json` carries a real vendor filename and address in `orig` fields alongside the redacted `text` fields); 124 storefront HTML files that name Tacombi, including `about/index.html:78` JSON-LD `worksFor`; and the invention-assignment / moonlighting / confidentiality clauses of an employment agreement no agent has seen. Vendor-side confidentiality on negotiated pricing (Baldor, Chefs' Warehouse, Pat LaFrieda) is a third party's interest that consent from the restaurant does not waive.
neglected.consequence: Authorisation to publish one month does not retroactively authorise fifteen months of product development on the employer's confidential vendor pricing, and it answers nothing about whether Muntin's IP is the founder's to sell. An invention-assignment clause would make the whole strategy moot. The public employment disclosure across 124 pages means the discovery cost for Tacombi's ownership is one search.

neglected.issue: Hand-invoicing walks straight into three different DMV sales-tax regimes with no tax engine
neglected.evidence: Maryland HB 352 (signed 2025-05-20, effective 2025-07-01) imposes 3% sales and use tax on data/IT services (NAICS 518, 519, 5415) and repeals the B2B and customised-software exemptions; SaaS for individual use stays at 6%. DC taxes "data processing services," defined by its Office of Tax and Revenue to include "the processing of information for compilation and production of records" and "payroll and business accounting," at 6% rising to 7% on 2026-10-01. [UNVERIFIED — confirm with a Maryland/DC SALT adviser.] The verdict specifies "$600/location/month, billed annually at $6,000, invoiced by hand … no billing code at all," and the buyer is DMV-clustered on purpose — Maryland, DC and Virginia in one cohort.
neglected.consequence: Deliberately removing Stripe removes the only tax calculation the company had. At 40 locations that is roughly $7-17k/year of tax that must be registered for, collected and remitted, and unremitted sales tax is generally a personal-liability item for a responsible officer regardless of the LLC. There is also a genuine bind: characterising the close as a professional service may take it out of the 3% data-services tax but pushes it toward the accountancy-licensing question, while characterising it as software does the reverse. The verdict never notices it is choosing.

neglected.issue: An outstanding written offer to a named list is revoked by one clause and never addressed
neglected.evidence: `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3162` and `:3319` publish "Founding rate — three months free, then $19 a month per location for as long as you stay" with `:3326` "Count me in as a founding member" and `:3331` "Founding members keep founder pricing"; the storefront repeats it on the home and `/ledger/` pages in EN and ES. `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md` A3 scopes counsel to draft `/legal/founding-member-terms` covering "the rate, the lock duration, transferability." The verdict's entire treatment is "Five posted prices come down and are replaced with 'Pricing set at the close of the pilot.'"
neglected.consequence: Anyone who joined that list accepted a specific, indefinite-term price. Replacing it with $600 — 31× — without a written communication is at best a bad first impression on the only warm list the company has, at worst promissory estoppel and an FTC §5 bait-and-switch pattern. The list size is unverifiable from the repos, which is itself the point: nobody knows how many people are owed an email.

recommendations.change: Rewrite the deliverable's vocabulary before it is spoken to anyone. Ban "signed," "opinion," "attest," "certify," "assurance," "audit," "workpaper" and "we stand behind" from the product, `/close/`, and the sales script. Replace with: "a dated, prepared statement of purchases, count and usage, produced from your records under a published method, with every estimate labelled." Keep the Ed25519 artefact but call it a tamper-evident record with a verification hash, and describe it as proving the file has not changed since delivery — not as a signature attesting the numbers are correct. Add, verbatim on every deliverable, the two Maryland safe-harbour sentences: no reference to SSARS, plus "The preparer of this report has not undergone and is not required to undergo peer review" and "Muntin is not a CPA firm; this is not an audit, review, compilation, or any other assurance engagement."
recommendations.why: Maryland's definition of practice reaches written opinions offering assurance on the correctness of information in a schedule or exhibit, with $5,000-per-violation civil penalties; the nonlicensee exception is for preparation *without the issuance of reports*, and COMAR 09.24.01.10 appears to give a compilation safe harbour keyed to exactly that peer-review sentence. The commercial promise — a dated close that foots or withholds — survives the rewrite intact. The framing does not have to.

recommendations.change: Add a Phase 0 legal gate of two written answers and stop the pivot until both are in hand: (a) a Maryland attorney or the Maryland Board of Public Accountancy on whether the deliverable as worded is a "report" under Bus. Occ. & Prof. Title 2 and whether COMAR 09.24.01.10's safe harbour applies to a food-cost/inventory schedule; (b) an employment attorney on the Tacombi agreement's invention-assignment, moonlighting and confidentiality clauses, scoped to cover the 919-invoice corpus's use for product development, not only publication of one specimen. Budget one flat-fee consult each.
recommendations.why: The verdict's Phase 0 lists a founder walk, an employer authorisation for the specimen, a red deploy and 72 corrections. Both of these questions are binary and both precede everything else: if the deliverable needs a licence the price is unsellable, and if the agreement assigns inventions the IP is not the founder's to sell. Nothing in the plan should consume founder-hours ahead of two answers that can void it.

recommendations.change: Resolve the agent-run exception desk before the price is posted. Pick one: (i) keep it and add Anthropic to `docs/sub-processors.md` with a real role description, amend DPA §6, ROPA A2 and the DPIA, run the 30-day clock before the first paid close, and immediately retire the unqualified "Your invoice content never reaches a language model" from `apps/web/lib/copy.ts:3082,3888,4067` and the 93 storefront pages in favour of a scoped claim ("no language model produces a number; a language model may read a failed invoice to author a rule, and you can see every rule"); or (ii) confine the desk to redacted layout structure with values stripped before any session sees it, prove it with a gate, and keep the absolute claim. Do not ship the verdict's version, which is (i) with only (ii)'s disclosures.
recommendations.why: `docs/sub-processors.md` states the LLM sub-processor was removed entirely and no third party processes invoice content, and the same document says that once paying customers exist the 30-day clock runs with no founder override. Disclosing the desk in prose on `/close/` while the DPA, sub-processor list and 93 pages say the opposite is the one failure this company cannot survive, because the buyer's CPA is the reader most likely to find it.

recommendations.change: Replace the click-through ToS with a real engagement letter for the first cohort, and treat the SaaS ToS as dead for this product. Minimum contents: parties and the confirmed legal entity; scope (which months, which locations, which vendors, what "a close" includes); an explicit statement that it is not an audit, review, compilation or attest engagement and not tax, accounting or legal advice; client responsibilities (complete invoice delivery, performing the physical count, timely review); a named, itemised limitations section covering the market-prior valuation basis, uncounted rows written at expected-on-hand, unreviewed purchase observations, and partial POS windows; **no third-party reliance** — the deliverable is for the client's internal management use only and may not be provided to a lender, investor, purchaser or insurer without Muntin's prior written consent and a separate acknowledgement; limitation of liability tied to fees; mutual confidentiality including vendor pricing; term, termination, and what happens to data; governing law and venue in the entity's actual state. Have counsel draft or review it — this outline is not a contract.
recommendations.why: An audit firm never delivers without one, and the verdict adopts the audit firm's sales posture while keeping the SaaS paperwork. The no-third-party-reliance clause is the single highest-value sentence in the document: it is what keeps a lender who relied on a signed inventory figure inside contract rather than in Restatement §552 territory where the 12-month fee cap does not reach.

recommendations.change: Get two insurance quotes before the first invoice, not after, and disclose the delivery mechanism honestly on both applications: a miscellaneous-professional / bookkeeper E&O and a tech E&O, each described as "prepared management reports of inventory valuation and food cost, no attest or assurance services, non-CPA." If any carrier declines or excludes on the basis of the wording, that decline is free market research on whether the framing crossed the line — treat it as a second opinion on recommendation 1. Make bound coverage a hard precondition for customer one.
recommendations.why: Solo bookkeeper E&O appears to run a few hundred dollars a year, but standard forms exclude services requiring a licence the insured lacks and commonly make public audit an ineligible practice area. Answering the application honestly is both the cheapest compliance test available and the only way the policy actually responds when a claim arrives; an inaccurate application is a voidable policy at exactly the moment it matters.

recommendations.change: Fix the entity and jurisdiction in one afternoon and make every document agree: confirm formation state, good standing and registered agent with SDAT (and Delaware if a Delaware entity exists); foreign-qualify wherever it transacts; then reconcile `LICENSE`, `docs/tos.md:135-137`, `terms.html:423,475,483,656`, the DPA, ROPA and privacy policy to one entity and one governing law. In the same pass, register for Maryland sales and use tax and get a written SALT opinion on whether a hand-invoiced monthly close is a 3% data/IT service, a 6% digital product, or a non-taxable professional service in MD, DC and VA — before an annual $6,000 invoice goes out to a DC or Virginia buyer.
recommendations.why: Two customer-facing documents currently name different states, and `docs/legal-counsel-kickoff.md:359` has had "confirmation an entity EXISTS" open as a founder to-do for roughly two months. Removing Stripe removes the tax engine; Maryland began taxing data/IT services at 3% on 2025-07-01 and DC's definition of taxable data processing explicitly names business accounting. Unremitted sales tax typically pierces the LLC to a responsible officer.

recommendations.change: Write to the founding list before any price change is published, in one plain email: the $19 founding offer is withdrawn, here is why, and here is what they get instead — either the founding rate honoured for anyone who joined before today, or first place in the pilot at a stated price. Then remove `foundingRate`, `foundingMemberLabel` and the ES mirrors from `apps/web/lib/copy.ts` and the storefront in the same commit, so the offer is not still live somewhere while the new price is posted.
recommendations.why: "Three months free, then $19 a month per location for as long as you stay" is a specific, indefinite-term written offer published in EN and ES on the home page, the `/ledger/` page and the in-product waitlist. The verdict revokes it in a subordinate clause. For a company whose only asset is credibility, silently withdrawing a written promise from the one warm list it has is a worse first act than any pricing error, and the fix costs one email.

recommendations.change: Before the specimen close is published, run a third-party confidentiality pass, not just an employer-consent pass: strip or generalise vendor identity and negotiated unit prices unless each named vendor's terms permit disclosure, and redact the remaining real Tacombi strings in `services/extract/tests/golden/real_fixtures/` (e.g. `fresco_merged_header.json`, whose `orig` fields still carry the unredacted vendor name and address while the sibling `text` fields are masked). Publish the method and the exception types in full; publish the prices only in ranges or as index-relative moves.
recommendations.why: The verdict's repair — "written authorization from ownership, or a redacted specimen, or a consenting third restaurant" — treats the restaurant as the only party with an interest. Baldor, Chefs' Warehouse and Pat LaFrieda negotiated pricing is the vendors' confidential information too, and the restaurant cannot waive it. Publishing the specimen is also what makes someone go look at the repo, which is exactly when unredacted fixtures become a problem rather than a note in an audit.

review.wouldChange: One written answer, from a Maryland attorney or from the Maryland Board of Public Accountancy itself, to a single question: "Is a dated, monthly statement of inventory valuation and food cost, prepared for a fee by a non-CPA from a client's own invoices and physical count, delivered with a preparer's signature and the sentence 'the preparer has not undergone and is not required to undergo peer review,' the issuance of a report under Bus. Occ. & Prof. Title 2 — and does COMAR 09.24.01.10's compilation safe harbour reach it?" If the answer is that the safe-harbour wording clears it, my verdict moves to ENDORSE_WITH_CONDITIONS and the remaining items are ordinary business hygiene. If the answer is that a signed statement of inventory valuation is a report regardless of the disclaimer, the strategy's central artefact cannot be sold at all in its current form and the seat's verdict becomes REJECT-as-framed. Obtaining it is cheap two ways: a one-hour flat-fee consult with a Maryland business attorney (roughly $250-500, unverified), or a written request for guidance to the Board of Public Accountancy at the Maryland Department of Labor, which costs nothing but a letter and produces the more authoritative answer. Ask it with the exact deliverable wording attached — the answer turns entirely on the words, which is why the wording must be settled before the question is asked.

title: Scale, Ambition & the Shape of the Company

review.seat: Scale, Ambition & the Shape of the Company
review.thesis: The $288K ceiling is not a fact about this asset base — it is a consequence of one chosen delivery model, and the verdict presents it as though it were arithmetic. Market size never binds: there were 412,498 independent US restaurants at end-2025 (external, secondary), so even a low-single-digit specialty-vendor share is tens of thousands of locations. What binds is that the close is hand-delivered. Worse, the ceiling and the capacity limit arrive at the same instant: the verdict's 13.3 h/month counts close review only (20 min x 40 locations) and nothing else. Add support, onboarding, hand-invoicing, and replacement selling at even 20% churn and steady state is ~23 h/month against a 13-26 band — so at exactly the point the business stops growing, it has consumed the entire founder budget and has zero surplus hours to fund an escape. That is the trap mechanism, and it is structural, not attitudinal. Meanwhile the one asset in either repo with genuine returns to scale is never named: the cross-tenant community template pool (migrations 0013/0056/0057, services/extract/community_pool.py, engine flag EXTRACT_COMMUNITY_POOL default-ON at engine_pkg/assemble.py:802, per-org opt-in default-off). Six repair slices already landed — row-invariant column_v2, held-out lift gate, supersession, operator-correction retirement — and the sole remaining gate is real-invoice layout coverage. A rule authored once serves every customer thereafter; forty customers ever starves the only mechanism whose marginal cost declines. The verdict's own buyer decision makes that gate cheap and it does not notice: the roadmap wanted "the top ~10 BROADLINER layouts," but the chosen buyer has zero broadliners, and VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:213-224 already measures the corpus's top seven specialty vendors at 79-93% reconcile. The same re-scoping un-parks /try — a stranger dropping their own invoice into the deterministic engine, already built, Turnstile'd, budget-broken, no-persistence-gated (ADR-007) — which is a strictly stronger public falsifier and acquisition surface than the /tools/pack-check/ the verdict proposes building. On the two branches: (a) a deliberate $250-300K, ~23 h/month service business is a genuinely excellent outcome at roughly $1,000 per founder-hour and I would endorse it if the founder says that is what he wants; (b) a larger company is available and its wedge is not the close but the specialty-vendor extraction layer nobody serves, with the close as its first application. The verdict is wrong only in presenting (a) as the honest ceiling rather than as a choice, in hard-capping at forty by public commitment in the one company that cannot break a public commitment, and in taking several branch-asymmetric kills without labelling them as such.

neglected.issue: The founder-hour ceiling counts close review only; adding the rest of hand-delivery puts steady state at the top of the budget, leaving zero surplus to ever escape the model
neglected.evidence: The verdict's own figure is '≈20 founder-minutes of close review × 40 locations = 13.3 h/month against 13-26 available'. That excludes per-customer support, onboarding a new customer's vendor layouts, hand-invoicing, and replacement selling. Modelled at 20 customers (2 loc avg): close 13.3 + support (20 min/cust) 6.7 + invoicing 0.8 + replacement sales at 20% churn 1.0 + onboarding 1.3 = ~23.2 h/month. The 13 h/month floor of the founder's own band is crossed at ~24 locations (~12 customers), less than a third of the way to the ceiling. Nothing named `desk_minutes`, `deskMinutes` or `close_minutes` exists anywhere in either repo — the one number the verdict says decides everything is not instrumented.
neglected.consequence: The plan reaches its revenue ceiling and its capacity ceiling simultaneously. There is never a month in which the business generates spare founder-hours, which is the only resource that could fund productization. The small version is therefore a trap by construction, not by temperament.

neglected.issue: The only asset with declining marginal cost — the cross-tenant community template pool — is never mentioned, and a 40-customer cap starves it
neglected.evidence: infra/postgres/migrations/0013_community_templates.sql (the pool, deliberately the one table without RLS because it is global by construction), 0056 supersession, 0057 distinct-org rejection counter; services/extract/community_pool.py; the fan applied at engine_pkg/assemble.py:802 with EXTRACT_COMMUNITY_POOL default=True; per-org opt-in default OFF (docs/community-templates.md, 'Default posture: Off'). docs/plans/first-try-reliability-roadmap.md logs six landed repair slices including the row-invariant column_v2 that fixed the fatal 'pooled fingerprint identifies a CELL not a COLUMN' defect, plus a held-out lift gate and operator-correction retirement. services/extract/cli/publish_community_seed.py lets the founder author rules once and pre-fill every opted-in org's FIRST invoice from that vendor.
neglected.consequence: The verdict's own claim that 'marginal cost scales with distinct vendor layouts, not with invoices or customers' is true only if this pool is live and populated. As written the plan neither activates it nor reaches the customer count at which pooled contribution compounds — so the economics it asserts are the economics of a mechanism it leaves dark.

neglected.issue: The verdict's buyer choice makes the parked /try demo cheap to un-park, and the verdict instead proposes building a weaker falsifier
neglected.evidence: docs/plans/first-try-reliability-roadmap.md: the one remaining un-park gate is '(a) real-invoice coverage… (i) the actual top-~10 broadliner layouts'. The verdict's buyer is defined by 'zero or one broadliner' and the corpus contains zero Sysco/US Foods/PFG. services/extract/VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:213-224 already measures i_halper 93.2%, chefs_warehouse 92.1%, baldor 89.7%, pat_lafrieda 87.5%, edward_don 85.7%, fresco 83.1%, montgomery_county_dlc 79.4% on the 919-doc corpus. ADR-007 records /try as BUILT and hardened (5MB cap, per-IP/ASN limits, $50/day budget breaker, Turnstile, replay cache, phone-photo downscale, CI-gated no-persistence), un-gating being 'a single flag flip'.
neglected.consequence: The verdict proposes /tools/pack-check/ as 'the one falsifier a stranger can actually execute' while a stronger one — the stranger's OWN invoice, read by the same deterministic engine — sits behind a gate its own buyer decision just made satisfiable. It also gives up the only acquisition surface that works without founder hours, in a plan whose scarcest resource is founder hours.

neglected.issue: $600/location is set against a misread competitive anchor, and realized discounting collapses the ceiling
neglected.evidence: Search results as of Aug 2026 (UNVERIFIED, secondary aggregator pages) report MarginEdge at $350/location/month flat with unlimited invoice processing and bill pay included, $250 one-time setup, and $660-$1,650/month for two-to-five locations with consolidated daily P&L. Muntin at $600/location quotes a 3-location buyer $1,800/month against roughly $990. The '$350-500 demonstrated willingness to pay' the verdict leans on is willingness to pay for the incumbent's full bundle, not evidence of $600 for a narrower monthly deliverable.
neglected.consequence: Multi-location buyers — the ones who make 40 locations reachable at 20 customers — see the worst relative price, so the mix skews to single-location buyers and the location count per customer falls. Every 25 points of realized discount removes ~$72K from a $288K ceiling, and the ceiling is already the plan's entire upside.

neglected.issue: The plan converts a capacity estimate into a public commitment, in the one company whose sole asset is that its statements hold
neglected.evidence: The verdict specifies 'Cohort hard-capped at 10 for the pilot and ~40 ever' alongside a storefront that replaces five posted prices with 'Pricing set at the close of the pilot' — i.e. the cap sits in the same public register as the price. The doctrine adopted wholesale is that credibility is the only asset the company has.

review.thesis: The verdict sells a signed, dated deliverable and the deliverable does not exist as an object anywhere in the product. `PeriodSnapshot` (`apps/api/src/lib/inventory-period-store.ts:14-38`) has no signature, no close date, no `delivered_at`, no version and no `supersedes`; it is written as a synchronous side effect of the operator pressing submit (`apps/api/src/routes/inventory.ts:608`), so there is no seat in the flow where a human reviews, withholds, or signs — the thing being sold is the one thing not built. The only Ed25519 signing in the codebase signs an invoice-package manifest (`apps/api/src/routes/accountant-handoffs.ts:858-870`), attesting "these are the files," not "these four legs foot," and the `pdfs` and `accountant` delivery shapes still return 503 (`accountant-handoffs.ts:51,289`). Second, the schedule is the worst one a one-person shop can choose: "your month closes on the second Tuesday" synchronizes all forty closes into the same 5-9 day window after month-end counts — the verdict's own 13.3 h/month budget is 1.9 hours a day for seven consecutive days, in the same week as the founder's own restaurant month-end, and 13.3 h is 51-102% of the 13-26 h/month that must also cover onboarding, support, sales, engineering, the Cost Index and the storefront. Third, the commercial argument — "half the labor at nearly twice the sticker," the count shrunk by Tier-2, Tier-3 and the market prior — has no code path: nothing substitutes a derived value for a counted ending QUANTITY (the market prior only prices what was already counted), and the honesty ladder actively punishes the attempt, since any estimated item forces `confidence = "medium"` and `countedShare < 0.5` forces `"low"` (`inventory-reconcile.ts:296-313`). So the plan's own machine will stamp "medium" on a deliverable sold as an audit opinion, every month, for every customer. Fourth, the amortization claim that justifies DMV clustering — "marginal cost scales with distinct vendor layouts, not with customers" — is false as built: templates are keyed `(org_id, vendor_id, layout_hash, field_path)` (`services/extract/template_store.py:73`) and line-item rules need four confirmations to promote (`template_store.py:100`), so every new customer re-pays 32-48 hand-reviewed invoices for vendors Muntin has already templated hundreds of times; the only cross-org path is an opt-in-both-ways community pool that is off by default (`apps/api/src/routes/community-templates.ts:19-30`). Fifth, onboarding is roughly 60-75 days to a first correct close and nobody scoped it — the baseline count sheet is built only from purchases inside the window (`inventory.ts:295-330`), so a real Beginning leg needs one full purchase month first — while `docs/tos.md:68` already promises pro-rated annual refunds, meaning a customer can cancel before the first deliverable and recover most of a $6,000-$12,000 prepay after the founder has spent the entire onboarding cost. Sixth, there is no support function and the runbooks say so out loud: `runbooks/slos.md:78` "we do not yet sell SLAs," `runbooks/incident-response.md:22` "founder is sole on-call" with the pager to be configured "on first day of paid beta," and both incident and extraction drills logged as "Not yet executed" — a P2 one-hour first response is a promise a man on a restaurant floor cannot keep. The good news is that the desk load is far more compressible than the verdict assumes: 44.5% of the entire exception queue comes from 12.6% of documents, all of them non-food vendors (Cintas 54.3%, Staples 37.5%, Cozzini 20.8% — `VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:219-228`), and two measured, tested flags that cut desk minutes are simply off in production. Fix the schedule, build the close object, scope the ledger to food, flip the flags, and this is deliverable at ten to twenty locations; leave them and the second Tuesday is the date the company misses in public.

neglected.evidence: From the per-vendor table at `services/extract/VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:219-228`: weighted reconcile across the ten vendors is 83.1% (n=533, ~90 failures). Cintas (54.3%, n=35), Staples (37.5%, n=8) and Cozzini Bros (20.8%, n=24) are 67 documents (12.6%) but 40 of the ~90 failures (44.5%). Excluding them lifts reconcile to 89.3%. Separately, `EXTRACT_MULTI_TABLE_HARVEST` defaults to False (`services/extract/engine_pkg/orchestrate.py:1112`) and `services/extract/README.md:138` records that with it off "chefswarehouse loses ~67% of its rows" — the #2 vendor in the buyer's own defined mix — while flipping it recovered +1011 line items with the reconcile rate unchanged. `EXTRACT_VENDOR_TRUST_ACTIVE` (`services/extract/main.py:120`) holds a measured 24%→62% first-pass improvement and requires `=="1"`, set nowhere.

neglected.issue: There is no support function, no sellable SLA, no drilled on-call and no status component for the thing being sold.
neglected.evidence: `runbooks/slos.md:78-80`: "Per-customer SLAs. We do not yet sell SLAs; the private-beta SLOs are operator-facing best-effort." `runbooks/incident-response.md:12-16` posts P1 15-minute / P2 1-hour / P3 4-business-hour first responses; `:22-26` says the founder is sole on-call and that the BetterStack pager and SMS backup "are set up in BetterStack on first day of paid beta" — i.e. not set up. neglected.consequence: At forty customers depending on a monthly number, inbound will be dominated by three predictable classes — "why is my number qualified," "this vendor's invoice is wrong," and "my CPA has a question" — each landing in the close week, the one week with zero slack. Publishing response times a person on a restaurant shift cannot honor converts a support gap into a broken promise.

neglected.issue: No restatement policy, credit memos structurally arrive after the close date, and the per-location price sells into the one shape that is arithmetically broken.
neglected.evidence: `PeriodSnapshot` has no `supersedes` or version column (`inventory-period-store.ts:14-38`); `write()` appends and `latestForLocation()` returns most-recent, so a corrected close silently shadows the signed one with no restatement record. Credit memos are already dropped from `line_item_observations` (documented defect), and a credit issued days after month-end cannot land before a second-Tuesday signature. `apps/api/src/lib/inventory-purchases-store.ts:19-20` states plainly "No location filter: invoices are not tied to a location_key," while counts and count sheets are per-location — and the verdict prices per location at a 1-3 location buyer.

recommendations.change: Kill the synchronized "second Tuesday." Replace it with a per-customer close slot assigned at signature — "your close is delivered within five business days of us receiving your count" — and spread slots across the month so no more than two or three closes fall in any week. Publish the customer's own date on their account page, not a company-wide date on the storefront.
recommendations.why: A single public date compresses the entire book into the one week the founder has least capacity, in the same week his employer closes its month. Staggering is why accounting firms have staggered year-ends. It costs nothing, preserves the whole positioning (a fixed, promised date MarginEdge's rolling turnaround cannot match), and converts a guaranteed public miss into a smoothable load.

recommendations.change: Instrument `desk_minutes_per_close` before selling anything. Add `review_started_at`/`reviewed_at` to the extractions store and a `prepared_at`/`signed_at`/`delivered_at` triple to the close record, and report minutes per close from customer one. Today those fields exist nowhere in `apps/api/src`.
recommendations.why: The verdict names `desk_minutes_per_close` as "the one number that decides whether it is more than" a $288K business, and then adds no apparatus to measure it. Every capacity claim in the plan — 13.3 h/month, forty locations, the honest one-founder ceiling — is an unmeasured assertion in a company whose brand is not publishing numbers it cannot stand behind.

recommendations.change: Build the close as a first-class object before the pilot opens: a `closes` row with period, location, `prepared_at`, `reviewed_by`, `signed_at`, `signature`, `withheld[]` with reasons, `supersedes_close_id`, `delivered_at`, and a durable (not 7-day, not single-use) share link for the CPA. Count submit produces a DRAFT close; only a signature publishes a number. Restatement is a new close that names its predecessor.
recommendations.why: The unit of value has no representation in the schema, the count-submit path prints a number with no human in it (`inventory.ts:608`), and there is no restatement record — which credit memos guarantee will be needed every month. Selling an audit opinion without a signing step, a withhold record and a restatement chain is selling the one thing that cannot be produced.

recommendations.change: Scope the food-cost ledger to food vendors. Classify vendors at onboarding and exclude linen, uniform, knife-route, office-supply and equipment vendors from the Purchases leg, the count sheet and the exception desk — showing them in a separate, unpriced "other spend" list.
recommendations.why: Cintas, Staples and Cozzini Bros are 12.6% of documents and 44.5% of exception failures (VENDOR-TEMPLATE-KEY.md:219-228); removing them lifts reconcile from 83.1% to 89.3% and cuts desk minutes roughly in half at zero cost to the number being sold. It also makes the Purchases leg correct: knife sharpening is not food cost, and including it inflates usage.

recommendations.change: Flip `EXTRACT_MULTI_TABLE_HARVEST` and `EXTRACT_VENDOR_TRUST_ACTIVE` in a measured pilot on the founder's own corpus during the Phase-0 walk, and record the desk-minute delta. Both are built, tested and validated; both default off (`orchestrate.py:1112`, `main.py:120`).
recommendations.why: With multi-table harvest off, Chefs' Warehouse — the second-largest vendor in the buyer profile the verdict itself defines — drops ~67% of its rows into manual review (README.md:138). Vendor trust holds a measured 24%→62% first-pass improvement. These are the two largest single levers on delivery cost in the entire company and they appear in none of the verdict's four phases.

recommendations.change: Publish an honest onboarding term and stop charging against it: the annual term starts at the FIRST SIGNED CLOSE, not at signature. Months 0-1 are a named, unbilled ramp with published milestones (vendors templated, catalog mapped, baseline count taken, net-sales source connected). Rewrite `docs/tos.md:61-69` so the pro-rated-refund clause cannot be exercised against work already spent.
recommendations.why: A real Beginning leg requires one full purchase month before the baseline count is complete (`inventory.ts:295-330`), and 8-12 vendors need 32-48 hand-reviewed invoices to train (`template_store.py:100`) — so the first correct close is ~60-75 days out. Taking $6,000-$12,000 up front for a deliverable that cannot arrive for two months, against a pro-rated refund promise, is the single largest uncompensated risk in the plan and it is entirely avoidable.

recommendations.change: Design the minimum support function and publish only what a person on a shift can honor: one channel (hello@), next-business-day response, two-business-day during close week, an explicit "we do not operate a pager" statement, and a make-good defined as a free month rather than a cash credit. Delete or scope the P1/P2/P3 response times in `incident-response.md` to internal use until a second person exists.
recommendations.why: `slos.md:78` already admits no SLA is sold; `incident-response.md:22` admits a single on-call whose pager is unconfigured and whose drills read "Not yet executed." Publishing 15-minute and 1-hour first responses is the same class of error as publishing a BLS index as $393/lb — a number the company cannot stand behind. An honest, unimpressive support promise is worth more here than an impressive one that fails in the close week.

recommendations.change: Cap the pilot by CONCURRENT CLOSES, not by locations-ever. Start at five locations, gate every expansion on two measured facts — desk minutes per close and minutes of inbound support per close — and only then decide the ceiling. Separately, put the scale question to the founder in these terms: an audit opinion requires a signer and therefore cannot scale past one calendar; a closed month can. If the ambition is scale, the signature must move to the METHOD (the limits register, the gates, the published refusals) rather than to each month's number.
recommendations.why: At 20 min/close the ceiling is 40 locations only if support, onboarding, sales and engineering are all zero. At a realistic 45-90 min the honest ceiling is 10-20 locations, i.e. $72K-$144K/year — which changes the answer to the unresolved scale question in both directions. Neither branch is served by an ops model whose only throughput lever is the founder's calendar, and nobody has said so.

review.wouldChange: The single fact that would most change this verdict is **measured desk minutes and support minutes for one real close of a customer who is not Don** — specifically: (a) minutes of founder time to clear the exception queue, review the reconciliation notes, decide withhold-vs-publish, and sign; (b) minutes of inbound questions in the fourteen days after delivery. It can be obtained cheaply and almost immediately: during the Phase-0 walk the founder should run his own two Tacombi locations through the PRODUCT path (not the Mac CLIs) with a stopwatch and a plain text log, then repeat it once with a single friendly second restaurant at zero price. That is roughly two evenings plus one month of elapsed time, and it costs nothing but the founder's attention. If desk time lands under ~25 minutes per close and support under ~15 minutes per customer-month, forty locations is defensible and my verdict softens to ENDORSE_WITH_CONDITIONS on the delivery items alone. If it lands north of ~60 minutes — which the org-scoped template training, the non-food exception concentration and the medium-confidence explanations all suggest it will for the first year — then the honest ceiling is ten to twenty locations, the second-Tuesday promise must be staggered before it is ever published, and the price/cohort arithmetic in the verdict needs rebuilding rather than repair.

title: The Fate of the Cost Index and the Free Data Line

review.seat: The Fate of the Cost Index and the Free Data Line
review.thesis: The Cost Index has exactly one load-bearing job under "Muntin sells a closed month," and the verdict never names it: it is the published basis of the market-prior rung in the valuation ladder — the input that lets a close value a no-invoice item, which is the whole commercial argument that the count gets shrunk rather than performed. Everything else the verdict gestures at is either false or unearned. It is not a moat: 100% of the 2,020 live-captured observations come from a single agency (USDA), `data/cost-index-health.json#summary` reports `highEligible: 0` against 20 medium / 62 low / 18 directional, the bulk export is CC0 and the methodology, weighting and shippable bar are all published — one HTTP GET reproduces it, and no ADR in either repo asks whether a competitor with distribution could. It is not a compounding citation asset either: `data/cost-index-editions.json` holds four frozen editions, the last `asOf 2026-07-06`, 32 days behind data at 2026-08-05, and it is appended only by a `workflow_dispatch`-only job that defaults to dry-run — the raw JSON compounds, the dated publication chain does not. The scale question the orchestrator flagged bites hardest here: a 40-customer business needs a 24-slug honest reference and nothing more, while a "toe to toe with the largest" business would need exactly the citation-capture program the verdict killed, and the founder cannot fund both — the verdict's ambiguity defaults the choice to "maintain 100 badly," which is the one option that serves neither branch. The maintenance arithmetic is decisive: directly attributable lines in the audit's own obligation ledger (dispatch 10, picker red 1, frozen-series triage 4, ADR-013 datasets 2, ingredient-state-record 0.5, cross-repo re-vendor 1) total 18.5 h/month before any share of gate upkeep, deploy-red clearing or the 142 `es/cost-index` pages — against a measured capacity of 13-26 h/month of which ~10% of maintenance was actually paid in the last thirty days. The Index alone is 42-47% of the company's total obligation and carries zero revenue mechanism. Worse, it is currently the thing that stops the company shipping: `cost-index-refresh.yml:99` rebuilds `data/cost-index-picker.js`, the `git add` allowlist at :302-311 omits it, `:313 git checkout -- .` discards it, and `node scripts/check-cost-index-picker.mjs` fails at HEAD right now — so the Index reds the storefront deploy every Mon/Wed/Fri, and Phase 0's "clear the red deploy" is written as a one-time act against a recurring cause. The honesty debt is also worse than the verdict recorded and concentrated in places it did not look: `basket.asOf` is 2026-06-01 with `coverage: 1` and `confidence: "medium"` while `_lastReviewed` reads 2026-08-05, 17.8% of basket weight sits on frozen contributors, and `/cost-index/shrimp/` publicly refuses to publish a shrimp price while the basket quietly uses shrimp's 2026-06-01 trend as a contributor. My position: keep the Index, shrink it to the twenty-four slugs the product actually consumes, retire the rest through ADR-021's machinery that has never once fired, kill the hand-written monthly dispatch, and move the CPA conversation to week one — because that single conversation, not any amount of correction work, decides whether this asset has a job at all.

title: The Financial Model — build it, do not assert it

review.seat: The Financial Model — built from the repos, committed at /home/user/potentially-profitable/docs/handoff/bones/finance-model.{md,json,py}
review.thesis: I built the model nobody built, and the strategy does not survive contact with its own arithmetic. The headline ceiling is wrong twice over. First, "$600/location/month, billed annually at $6,000" and "40 × $600 = $288K ARR" cannot both be true — $6,000/yr is $500/month, so the invoiced ceiling is $240,000, and the annual prepay is a 16.7% discount never named as one. Second, and larger: the 13.3 founder-hours/month that justifies the 40-location cap counts close review ONLY. Add exception-desk rule review (a signature means the founder read the rules), per-customer support and hand-invoicing, platform upkeep (306 cost-index pages, 21 manual builders, agent-PR review, keeping a deploy green that currently exits 1), and onboarding for a buyer explicitly defined as carrying 8-12 specialty vendors — and at the verdict's own 20-minute close the servable ceiling falls from 40 locations to 19.8, with zero hours left to sell the twentieth. Costs are small and knowable: $248-892/month recurring (Fly $34 effective on the founder's own June bill, Neon, Cloudflare Workers Paid, KMS, Resend, BetterStack, domains) plus $3,500-11,500/year of E&O, counsel, accounting and store fees — but the single largest line, the agent workforce that authored 491 of 584 product commits and is supposed to RUN the exception desk, appears in no repo, no budget, and no question asked of the founder in 100+ agents. Cash timing is worse than what it replaced: the verdict killed the November GA because three-months-free landed the first charge in mid-February (season 0.917), then scheduled Phase 3 at weeks 10-13 and hand-invoices on signature — first cash lands 2027-01, season 0.913, the actual worst month of the restaurant year. Under its own stated "invoice in the May-August peak" policy a November signature gets six months of signed closes free and eight months before cash, and worst cash drops from -$11,735 to -$24,262. Unit economics are excellent when they work — 79-92% gross margin, infrastructure covered by two locations forever — but that is exactly why the model is not a business plan: the residual at the service ceiling ranges from $224/year to $280,000/year on one parameter, desk_minutes_per_close, which returns zero grep hits in either repo and which the verdict proposes to measure from customer one, i.e. after the price is set. Price is the least sensitive lever in the whole model (2.5× on price moves the BASE ceiling 2.5×; 45→12 desk-minutes moves it 14×), and this company has spent fifteen months and five posted prices arguing about it. Finally, the model never makes quitting rational, and that is structural: the plan is engineered to be servable in 13-26 hours/month, which is precisely what makes it unable to become the founder's job — quitting frees ~140 hours into a business whose ceiling is a policy cap of 40 locations, converting a 90%-margin side business into a full-time job at identical revenue.

review.seat: Execution Feasibility — does the plan survive the calendar?
review.thesis: The strategy is executable; the plan built to execute it is not yet, and the reason is not capacity — it is that the plan's own spine is uncommitted and its verify contract already fails on item one. As of this session, `data/queue.json`, `docs/handoff/QUEUE.md` and `scripts/check-queue.mjs` are all untracked (`git status --porcelain` shows `??` on each), `docs/editorial/decisions/ADR-022-the-queue.md` — cited in QUEUE.md's header as the strategy of record — does not exist on disk at all, and `.claude/hooks/` is an empty directory in both repos even though `check-gate-coverage.mjs:96` asserts in the present tense that check-queue "is invoked instead by .claude/hooks/session-start.sh in BOTH repos." That is line 852 reproduced inside the registry whose entire job is to prevent line 852, on the day the doctrine "pay the honesty debt in full" was adopted. Second, the queue's central promise — "closed only by a verify command that exited 0" — is already broken on Q-007: `check-src-sentinel.mjs` exits 0 today reporting `UNANCHORED=138 DRIFT=21 (ratchet holding)`, while Q-007's own doneWhen demands "zero unanchored annotations"; `--done` runs verify, not doneWhen, so the highest-priority honesty item can be certified closed with 138 unverifiable citations and one sign-flipped published market read still live. Third, the gate rewards the wrong act: `unclaimedHigh()` filters to ready-and-unblocked, so claiming ten items in one command greens it for seven days with zero work done, and *closing* Q-001 unblocks Q-020/21/22/24 and immediately re-reds it — doing the single most valuable thing in the plan makes the only visible health signal worse. Fourth, two of the four Phase-0 founder items are misdiagnosed: all five builders Q-005 names pass `--check` here today (exit 0 each), and Q-006's premise that the keys are missing is falsified by `muntin-cost-index-bot` committing measured reads to main on 2026-08-03 and 2026-08-05 through a workflow every step of which is guarded by `if: steps.keys.outputs.configured == 'true'` — while Q-006's verify demands a ≤2-day-old commit to `data/cost-index-editions.json`, a file appended once per monthly edition that last moved 2026-07-06, so the item cannot be closed by doing it. Fifth, nothing in the queue deploys the product: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml` is four `echo "TODO(B-priv-6)"` stubs behind a two-person approval gate at a one-person company, and its web step still names Vercel while CLAUDE.md says OpenNext/Cloudflare — so the twenty agent-hours of Q-020/21/22/24 reach zero customers until an unqueued, undelegatable founder runs `deploy-api.sh` and `deploy:cf` from his Mac, and Q-030's specimen is then built from a close no buyer can obtain. Sixth, the calendar contradicts the pricing doctrine: "$6,000 billed annually, hand-invoiced, in the May-August seasonal peak" cannot be honored by a Phase 3 that runs weeks 10-13 from 2026-08-07, i.e. 16 October to 6 November — the same off-peak, into-the-Jan-February-trough placement the verdict killed the 2026-11-13 GA for, and the next peak is May 2027. On raw hours the plan-only load (~15h queue + ~3h product deploys + ~5h PR review + ~5h August dispatch) is roughly 28h over eight weeks against 26-52 available and does fit; it fits only because it silently assumes the ~53h/month standing maintenance calendar is suspended, which no queue item does — with maintenance the eight-week demand is ~130h against 26-52, a 2.5-5× deficit. Two hard dates nobody scheduled land inside those eight weeks: `check-cost-index-dispatch-fresh.mjs` passes at 27 of 38 days today and reds around 16 August, demanding a hand-written monthly edition in week 2; and the vendored `cost-index-snapshot.json` (`_asOfRange: 2026-07-18..2026-07-28`, `STALE_AFTER_DAYS = 30`) puts 2 of 24 slugs at the 20-day warn line now and the last 18 over the cliff on 27 August, so a Q-001 walk that slips past week 3 measures a silently degraded valuation ladder and could abort the pilot on an artifact of a stale file.

title: The Completeness Seat — what no seat at this table covers

review.seat: The Completeness Seat — what no seat at this table covers
review.thesis: The spine is right and I am not attacking it: correctness before amplification, one price, a hard-capped cohort, employer authorization, no billing code, and the founder's own end-to-end walk in week one are all correct, and the reasoning that got there is the best thinking in this engagement. What the judge produced is a superb product-correctness plan wearing a company's clothes. Three of its own load-bearing words each require an artifact that does not exist and that no phase creates: "signed" needs an engagement letter and a liability position, "audit opinion" needs a licensing and reliance answer, and "hand-invoiced" needs an entity, a tax determination, and a refund policy that is not the retired studio's. The live public `terms.html` still governs a web-design studio — "if you hire the studio, the engagement letter governs," "the studio runs two builds at a time," Maryland law — and `check-positioning-drift.mjs` passes it at 0 violations because its vocabulary list hunts "wordpress" and "wix," not "studio," "proposal," and "care plan"; the gate the founder is proudest of cannot see the company's binding legal instrument. More seriously, the plan has no route to customer one. Across the whole verdict the words network, outbound, introduction, and cold appear zero times; acquisition is "an application page" and "~400 qualified readers" who arrive by no named mechanism, while `sourced-claims.json` records four DMV restaurants the founder has personally worked in — the only warm channel this company has, unnamed and unscreened for the employer conflict that makes it dangerous. Two structural questions went unasked by 100+ agents: there is no labor plan (succession appears zero times; "first hire" appears once, to dismiss it), so the $288K ceiling is a hiring decision presented as a physical constant; and there is no continuity plan, so ten customers who prepay $60,000 against a ToS promising pro-rated refunds are unsecured creditors of a man with a day job. Finally, and most likely to kill the plan on contact: the verdict never cites `docs/handoff/founder-vision.md`, where on 2026-07-11 the founder decided in his own words to *stop* foregrounding that it is one person — "I worry that if people know it's just me, they'll discount the product" — and this strategy makes the one person the product, signs his name to the number, and proposes to publish "a very good one-person business" as positioning. That is not a detail; it is the last recorded founder decision, silently overturned. Adopt the spine, revise the plan.

review.wouldChange: Whether Don's Tacombi employment agreement permits him to sell a paid food-cost service to independent restaurants in the DMV, and whether ownership will say so out loud. It is binary, it costs one reading of a document he already has plus one conversation, and it simultaneously gates the specimen close (the verdict's own non-negotiable graft), the buyer definition (DMV 1-3 location independents are Tacombi's competitive set), and the only realistic first-ten channel (his personal restaurant network). If the answer is no — a confidentiality, outside-activity, or non-solicit clause that reaches restaurant clients in his market — then the beachhead, the specimen, and the acquisition route all die at once and the strategy of record needs a different geography or a different buyer, not a different sequence. If the answer is yes in writing, the plan's single largest hole (no route to customer one) closes the same week. The second-cheapest fact, worth asking in the same sitting: what does he actually want this to be in five years, and how much of his own money is he willing to lose finding out — `runbooks/v6-pivot-plan.md:70` has him on record planning a $70-115k personal burn that nothing in either repo derives, and no seat has ever asked him whether that number is real.
